html:
Writing and registering user Python skills

A user skill is an independently authored Python component exposing one or more typed tools. SMTO imports it in a separate process, discovers its contracts, and adapts those tools into normal agent discovery, capability selection, permissions, execution receipts and job controls. It does not require a controller source edit.

Quick start

  1. Open Settings → User Skills, or /skills on your controller.

  2. Download Hello World and Python SDK.

  3. Extract the example. To edit and validate it locally, use Python 3.11 or later:

    python -m venv .venv
# Activate this environment using your platform's normal command.
python -m pip install ./smto_skill_sdk-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl
python -m smto_skill_sdk validate ./hello_world

  4. Review a folder on the controller host, or upload a ZIP containing skill.toml at its root. A folder on the browser's computer is not a controller path; upload its ZIP instead.

  5. Review the manifest and dependencies, acknowledge trusted code, and register. Wait for Registered. This installs dependencies and executes the factory and discovery methods in a temporary worker.

  6. Open Capabilities in chat and select Hello World for the conversation or globally. Ask the agent to greet a person with the skill.

The example exposes user_hello_world.greet(name) and returns:

{"message": "Hello, Ada!"}

Registration alone does not grant agent access. Existing capabilities and permissions still determine whether a tool may run.

Bundle and manifest

hello_world/
  skill.toml
  hello.py

schema_version = 1
id = "user_hello_world"
version = "1.0.0"
entrypoint = "hello:create_skill"
requires_python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = []

These are the complete required v1 manifest fields. IDs start with user_, use lowercase letters/digits/underscores, and cannot contain __. Tool names use the same characters without that prefix. SMTO combines the skill ID and tool name into a canonical ID; interface identifiers are separate from package versions.

entrypoint is a Python module and zero-argument factory, not an expression or shell command. The factory returns an IUnknownV1 implementation. Include local helper modules beside the entry module. Declare third-party dependencies as Python requirement strings, for example dependencies = ["requests==2.32.5"]. SMTO supplies the SDK; do not declare a replacement SDK dependency.

Each revision gets a managed virtual environment using the controller's genuine Python interpreter. Incompatible Python requirements fail installation; SMTO does not download another interpreter. Dependency installation may require network access. The dependency-free examples install from the bundled SDK wheel offline. The resolved dependency inventory appears in the registration API.

Folder registration makes a copy. Editing the original folder does not change an installed skill. ZIPs must not contain absolute paths, .., links, special files or duplicate paths. Limits: 16 MiB compressed, 64 MiB expanded, 2048 files. Folder snapshots omit .git, .venv, venv, bytecode caches and pytest caches. Keep configuration and credentials outside the bundle.

Mandatory interface

Import the public classes from smto_skill_sdk, never agent_runtime.

Interface Method Contract
IUnknownV1 query_interface(interface_id) Return the supported interface or None. The inherited implementation handles ordinary multiple inheritance.
ISkillV1 describe() -> SkillDescriptor Return ID, version, display name, description and optional instructions. ID/version must match the manifest.
ISkillV1 list_tools() -> list[ToolDescriptor] Return between 1 and 128 fixed tool declarations.
ISkillV1 initialize(context: SkillContext) -> None Open control resources without starting business operations.
ISkillV1 invoke(tool_name: str, arguments: dict, context: SkillContext) -> SkillResult Execute one authorized synchronous invocation.
ISkillV1 shutdown() -> None Release control resources. Do not cancel independently owned durable jobs.

Python abstract methods prevent incomplete implementations from being created. All v1 methods are synchronous. Discovery must be deterministic, bounded and free of business effects. SMTO checks method signatures, descriptors, schema syntax, identity and tool ownership before exposing any tools. Local SDK validation checks the Python interfaces; registration also performs full JSON Schema validation.

The interface constants are IID_UNKNOWN = "smto.IUnknown/1", IID_SKILL = "smto.ISkill/1", and IID_JOBS = "smto.IJobSkill/1". Every interface must resolve the same root identity; the supported set is fixed for that instance. Python manages references: there is no manual AddRef/Release. Changing a mandatory interface requires a new interface ID, independently of a skill's package version.

Tool declarations and results

ToolDescriptor has these fields:

Field Meaning
name, description Stable local name and a clear explanation of when/how to use the tool.
input_schema, output_schema JSON Schema 2020-12 objects describing arguments and successful result data. Only local schema references are supported.
effect read or write; defaults to write. Declare actual effects conservatively.
mode call or job; defaults to call. A job requires IJobSkillV1.
timeout_seconds Worker-call deadline, 1–3600 seconds; defaults to 120. A job tool's timeout bounds launch, not the job's lifetime.

Use additionalProperties: false for a precise input contract. Runtime control names such as background, detached, target, job_lifetime_seconds and __smto_* control fields cannot be business arguments.

Return SkillResult(data={...}) for success, or SkillResult(data={...}, error="Explanation") for a business error. Successful data is validated against the output schema. Exceptions, worker exits, malformed results and timeouts after dispatch preserve possible execution. SMTO does not replay an uncertain write. A schema mismatch cannot prove a write did not happen.

Only bounded JSON crosses the IPC boundary (1 MiB per frame). Printing goes to bounded worker diagnostics, not the tool result. Do not print credentials or put them into errors. A skill cannot supply its own SMTO authorization or receipts.

Context and configuration

SkillContext contains run_id, operation_id, state_dir (a Path), deadline (Unix seconds), and cancelled (a threading.Event). job_id aliases the launch's operation_id. Check context.cancelled.is_set() during lengthy calls. After a two-second cancellation grace period, SMTO can terminate an unresponsive worker.

Use state_dir for durable provider-handle mappings, namespaced by run/job identity. Do not depend on Python instance memory surviving a wait, restart or worker eviction. The worker pool is bounded; idle processes may be recreated.

The skill owns its configuration. Read author-managed environment variables or configuration files outside the installed source snapshot. Workers inherit the controller process environment; there is no SMTO credential injection or skill configuration form. Changing service environment variables generally requires restarting that service. Never modify the installed source directory.

Skills execute under the controller's OS account. This is trusted-code execution with process/dependency separation, not an OS security sandbox. The SDK exposes no agent loop, runtime objects or nested SMTO tool calls.

Optional durable jobs

Implement IJobSkillV1 in addition to ISkillV1, and declare mode="job":

class MySkill(ISkillV1, IJobSkillV1):
    # Implement the mandatory methods plus:
    def start_job(self, tool_name, arguments, context): ...
    def get_job(self, job_id, context): ...
    def cancel_job(self, job_id, context): ...
    def read_job_logs(self, job_id, cursor, context): ...

The first three methods return JobSnapshot. It contains job_id, state, active, optional result: SkillResult, optional progress, and log_bytes.

  • States: queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled, unknown.
  • Queued/running work has active=True. Terminal states require observed inactivity, active=False; successful jobs also require a validated result.
  • Use unknown and active=None when the outcome/liveness cannot be established.
  • progress uses the standard progress fields: availability, phase, label, and optional measurements. Measurements have id, label, unit, completed and optional total. Report measured counts, not estimated completion.
  • log_bytes is the current UTF-8 byte length, allowing output waits and final log capture. read_job_logs returns LogPage(text, next_offset, complete), at most 64 KiB. The cursor advances by the exact UTF-8 bytes returned.

SMTO saves launch intent before invoking start_job. Use context.job_id as the idempotency/correlation key and durably retain the underlying provider identity before acknowledging it. If the provider supports idempotency keys, pass it there. Never use status recovery as an opportunity to launch again.

The existing manage_job tool supports inspection, logs, waits, detachment and cancellation. External jobs do not accept terminal input. Final structured output is retained under result in the job's terminal receipt.

After a restart, SMTO recreates the control process at the original skill revision and calls get_job. It does not restore Python stacks or automatically invoke start_job again. The skill must reconnect to independently retained work or truthfully report interruption/uncertainty. A missing provider record does not prove that an external effect never happened. Cancellation must report observed termination, rather than merely acknowledging a cancel request.

Download Durable job example for an executable implementation. It retains a due time and greeting atomically, so status remains recoverable without keeping a thread alive. Real integrations persist and reconcile their provider's job handle.

Updates, disablement and recovery

Upload/register a changed bundle with the same skill ID to update it. Installation is staged and validated before publication; failures leave the active version unchanged. New runs use the newly installed revision. Existing and resumed runs use their recorded code/schema revisions throughout authorization and dispatch.

Disable blocks new invocations, including calls from previously accepted runs. Existing jobs remain inspectable/cancellable. Remove retires the installation; retained revisions support old runs and unresolved jobs. Re-enable restores availability without granting capabilities. Version data is retained conservatively; removal is not a disk-purge operation.

The settings store retains installation metadata. Code snapshots, environments and skill-owned state live in external-skills beside the controller state database. Back up that directory alongside controller state; ordinary metadata restoration does not recreate a missing environment or external provider state. To repair a missing environment, register the same original bundle again. A missing source or environment remains unavailable instead of silently substituting another version.

The registration page shows installation phases, failures and worker diagnostics. Management endpoints live under /api/agent/external-skills; they use the normal authenticated UI session and CSRF handling and are not advertised to the agent.

Development checks

Test schema errors, read/write permissions, cancellation, unexpected exceptions, worker loss, dependency isolation, update pinning and recovery before sharing a skill. For jobs, simulate a lost launch acknowledgement and ensure recovery only observes the existing job. Keep Hello World as the smallest conformance reference.
